Article states only one Malvaceae species was reported. Historical evidence narrows the lineage to Mollia: Darwin 1877 records long outer versus short inner stamen cohorts with different pollen colours and explicitly examined M. lepidota and M. speciosa; Müller 1883 repeats the Mollia pattern. Because those sources involve multiple Mollia species, they cannot identify which single species owned the review's 2010 report. Exact representative therefore remains OPEN rather than guessed.

Independent species-level resolution, not Table S1 transcription. Flora of North America / Hodgson's Bixaceae treatment describes Amoreuxia as having two dimorphic fertile stamen sets; A. wrightii specifically has shorter distal filaments with yellow anthers and longer proximal filaments with usually dark-red anthers. APG-style sources place Amoreuxia in Bixaceae, consistent with the review's merger of Cochlospermaceae into Bixaceae.

This is an independent pre-2010 resolution, not a claim that Supporting Table S1 was accessed.
